Compare indicators between survey rounds and between subgroups

Source: R/compare.R
bdhs_compare.Rd

Tests differences of indicators between BDHS rounds (for example the change in caesarean deliveries from 2017-18 to 2022) and between groups within a round (for example urban versus rural), with design-based standard errors, confidence intervals and z tests.

Usage

bdhs_compare(
  ...,
  indicators = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  rounds = c("consecutive", "first_last", "all"),
  groups = c("reference", "pairwise"),
  design_args = list()
)

Arguments

...

Either data frames of BDHS recode data (one per round, or one pooled data frame with a survey_id column, see bdhs_pool()), or bdhs_estimate objects from bdhs_estimate() (not a mix).

indicators

Indicator ids (see bdhs_indicator_list()). Required for data frames; for bdhs_estimate inputs it optionally selects indicators.

by

Optional single grouping variable. For bdhs_estimate inputs it is detected from the columns.

level

Confidence level of the intervals of the differences.

rounds

Which pairs of rounds to compare: "consecutive" (default), "first_last" or "all" pairs.

groups

Contrasts between groups within a round: "reference" (every group minus the first group, default) or "pairwise".

design_args

A list of further arguments passed to bdhs_design().

Value

A tibble of class bdhs_comparison with one row per comparison and columns comparison ("rounds" or "groups"), indicator, label, by (grouping variable or NA), survey_1, survey_2, group_1, group_2, estimate_1, estimate_2, difference (second minus first), se, ci_low, ci_high, z, p_value, years (between survey mid-points), annual_change and annual_change_se (per year; NA for group contrasts). Proportions are on the 0-100 scale, so differences are in percentage points.

Details

Between rounds. BDHS rounds are independent samples, so the difference \(d = \hat\theta_2 - \hat\theta_1\) has \(SE(d) = \sqrt{SE_1^2 + SE_2^2}\); \(z = d / SE(d)\) and the p-value is two-sided from the standard normal. The annualized change is \(d / (t_2 - t_1)\), where \(t\) is the mid-point of each survey's fieldwork (from bdhs_surveys), with standard error \(SE(d) / (t_2 - t_1)\). Rates (fertility, mortality) and medians use their jackknife standard errors.

Between groups within a round. Groups of the same survey are not independent (they share strata and clusters), so their estimates are computed jointly with survey::svyby() (covmat = TRUE) and the difference uses survey::svycontrast(), which accounts for the covariance. Indicators with all-women denominators use the ratio estimator of bdhs_estimate() with the all-woman factor of the by variable. Within-round contrasts need the microdata; they are not computed from bdhs_estimate objects, nor for rates and medians.

Divisions. Bangladesh had 5 divisions in 1993-94, 6 to 2007, 7 in 2011-2014 and 8 from 2017-18, and the codes of v024 changed. Comparing v024 (or division_surveyed) across rounds with different layouts compares different areas under the same name; a warning recommends the harmonized division_trend6 from bdhs_harmonize().

See also

bdhs_estimate(), bdhs_inequality(), bdhs_decompose().

Examples

kr17 <- bdhs_simulate(2017, "KR")
kr22 <- bdhs_simulate(2022, "KR")
bdhs_compare(kr17, kr22, indicators = "rh_del_csection")
#> # BDHS comparisons: 1 between rounds, 0 between groups | 95% CI
#> # A tibble: 1 × 19
#>   comparison indicator  label by    survey_1 survey_2 group_1 group_2 estimate_1
#>   <chr>      <chr>      <chr> <chr> <chr>    <chr>    <chr>   <chr>        <dbl>
#> 1 rounds     rh_del_cs… Deli… NA    BD2017D… BD2022D… NA      NA            33.7
#> # ℹ 10 more variables: estimate_2 <dbl>, difference <dbl>, se <dbl>,
#> #   ci_low <dbl>, ci_high <dbl>, z <dbl>, p_value <dbl>, years <dbl>,
#> #   annual_change <dbl>, annual_change_se <dbl>

# Urban-rural gap within each round and its change between rounds
bdhs_compare(kr17, kr22, indicators = "rh_del_csection", by = "v025")
#> # BDHS comparisons: 2 between rounds, 2 between groups | 95% CI
#> # A tibble: 4 × 19
#>   comparison indicator  label by    survey_1 survey_2 group_1 group_2 estimate_1
#>   <chr>      <chr>      <chr> <chr> <chr>    <chr>    <chr>   <chr>        <dbl>
#> 1 rounds     rh_del_cs… Deli… v025  BD2017D… BD2022D… urban   urban         36.2
#> 2 rounds     rh_del_cs… Deli… v025  BD2017D… BD2022D… rural   rural         31.8
#> 3 groups     rh_del_cs… Deli… v025  BD2017D… BD2017D… urban   rural         36.2
#> 4 groups     rh_del_cs… Deli… v025  BD2022D… BD2022D… urban   rural         29.2
#> # ℹ 10 more variables: estimate_2 <dbl>, difference <dbl>, se <dbl>,
#> #   ci_low <dbl>, ci_high <dbl>, z <dbl>, p_value <dbl>, years <dbl>,
#> #   annual_change <dbl>, annual_change_se <dbl>

# From saved estimates
e1 <- bdhs_estimate(kr17, "rh_del_facility")
e2 <- bdhs_estimate(kr22, "rh_del_facility")
bdhs_compare(e1, e2)
#> # BDHS comparisons: 1 between rounds, 0 between groups | 95% CI
#> # A tibble: 1 × 19
#>   comparison indicator  label by    survey_1 survey_2 group_1 group_2 estimate_1
#>   <chr>      <chr>      <chr> <chr> <chr>    <chr>    <chr>   <chr>        <dbl>
#> 1 rounds     rh_del_fa… Deli… NA    BD2017D… BD2022D… NA      NA            54.7
#> # ℹ 10 more variables: estimate_2 <dbl>, difference <dbl>, se <dbl>,
#> #   ci_low <dbl>, ci_high <dbl>, z <dbl>, p_value <dbl>, years <dbl>,
#> #   annual_change <dbl>, annual_change_se <dbl>
